blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence: - A plugin system for export formats, so that PDF, XLSX, XML and JSON exports can be added later by dropping a module in `src/export/plugins/`.
findings.recommendation: The Why is only "Accountants copy invoices one by one into their spreadsheet at the end of each month." — a single CSV route solves it. Drop the plugin system from What Changes, replace "Decision: Exports go through a plugin registry" in design.md (the rejected "single CSV function" is the simpler solution the Why calls for) and remove task 1.2 ("Plugin registry discovering `src/export/plugins/`"), which traces to no requirement of specs/invoice-export/spec.md. This also removes the unverified assumption that `registry.ts` can discover modules in `src/export/plugins/` at start-up once compiled by `tsc -p .`. A plugin system can be proposed in its own change when a second format is actually requested.
findings.title: A plugin system for future formats nobody asked for

findings.evidence: The settings page SHALL let a user choose their preferred export format among the installed plugins.
findings.location: specs/invoice-export/spec.md#Requirement: Users choose their export format
findings.recommendation: Nothing in the Why asks for a format preference, and with CSV as the only format the choice has no effect: the route is `GET /invoices.csv`, so the scenario "A preference" ("**WHEN** a user picks CSV / **THEN** exports use CSV") cannot fail and verifies nothing. Remove this requirement and its scenarios, the "A settings page where each user picks their preferred export format." line of proposal.md#What Changes, `web/src/settings/` from proposal.md#Impact, the last sentence of the design decision ("A settings page stores each user's preferred format.") and task 2.1. Note that it would also need a storage for the preference that the plan never describes, and a user-visible change absent from the release note.
findings.title: A per-user export-format settings page nobody asked for

findings.recommendation: The new route `GET /invoices.csv?month=YYYY-MM` exposes a whole month of invoices, with each customer's name, and neither the proposal nor the spec says who may call it (no "unauthorized" scenario): tick `security` and `personal-data` so that their experts review it, or give the reason on the line. While the settings page stays in scope (see R-skeptic-2), tick `user-interface` too — the plan modifies `web/src/settings/`.
findings.title: Domains the plan touches are all unticked, with no reason
